title: Gated stored-leaf birthday search on secp256k1, one processor with bank-selected memory, at 123.256664456028732

claims.statement: Gated grouped stored-leaf birthday search (proof.md) recovers x from uniform secp256k1 Q=[x]P w.p. >= 0.39 (Q=O gives x=0). The processor halts with no output unless a 128-bit RNDR u < K_GATE = 132738613357423514467234461755771470501 (p_gate ~ 0.390083725); else Phase-0 X-mining (E_mine <= 2^123.8587 insns; no output if a pool has < 4 valid pairs), then q1 = 103,079,062,500 batches in G = 6656 groups for 2^66 virtual generators, leaf records inserted into a hash table of 2^132 slots in 2^85 banks. lo_run >= 0.999785365708 (rounded down), (K_GATE/2^128) lo_run >= 0.39 (exact rationals, c21). E_total = 256 insns + p_gate E_run <= 2^123.256664456028732 units of 1000 AArch64 insns (E_run <= 2^124.614809 units, <= 56.7438 insns/leaf of S = 2^128.754203); memory <= 2^138.0001 B; pre <= 2^117.2094 units; no advice; a run does at most 2^170.5434 units (c55). Premise BM: one unmodified processor whose bulk memory is a memory-mapped device that no Arm system has. A select is counted stores and DSBs; the hash select, once a leaf, is 6 of them: two stores to enable cells put a bank on its window, DSB, accesses, DSB, two stores take it off. The gate that connects a bank while both cells are set is hardware; the count holds no instruction for it (proof.md premises, 2, 8).

experiments.purpose: Runs the leaf, Phase-0, hash-insert, Y-store and zeroing kernels on the specified memory device (kernels/a64.py Bank) at production digit and slot widths on sparse memory: select negative cases by name, the cell-clearing loop on a small device, counts of window accesses with exactly one bank and of calls that left the hash cells clear, hash contents and counts against a flat model, occupied-path cases, frames consumed where ystore stored them by two members, a planted collision, the same leaves in two chunks, a count of loads that return poison, gate, C132 bound and counts.
